 JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.25,000/- for the injuries suffered by her in a road accident dated 09.11.2017.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 09.11.2017 at about 11.45a.m., the petitioner and her husband were going on their Activa Honda two wheeler SCCH-25 bearing No.KA-04-HX-4788 towards Doddanakundi.

At that time a Car bearing No.KA-01-MM-4236 came with high speed, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed petitioner's two wheeler from the hind side and caused the accident.
Due to impact petitioner and her husband fell down and sustained injuries, spent around Rs.10,000/- towards medical expenses.
3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
The KR Puram Traffic Police, Bangalore have registered a case in Cr.No.0410/2017 against the driver/1st respondent of the Car bearing No.KA-01-MM-4326 for the offences p/u/Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC.

The 1 st respondent being the Driver, 2nd respondent being the owner and 3rd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are SCCH-25 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
4. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondent Nos.2 & 3 appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.
In spite of due service of summons the Respondent No.1 did not appear.
Hence, placed ex-parte.
5. Objection of the Respondent No.2.
This respondent denies the averments made in Para 1 to 22 of the petition.
Further denied the manner of accident, treatment, medical expenses, petitioner's work and earnings.
Further stated that the Car is insured with the 3 rd respondent vide policy bearing No.118000023326.
She has denied the compensation claimed by the petitioner.
6. Objection of the Respondent No.3.
The petition is not maintainable for non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of the MV Act.

It has contended that SCCH-25 the policy bearing No.118000023326 mentioned in the claim petition in Sudha Ravishankar vs Naveeen .N on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84711924/
2 respect of the private car does not tally with the records maintained by this respondent and false and fabricated one.

Further denied the involvement of the Car in the accident.
The driver of the Car did not have a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.

Further stated that the petitioner stopped two wheeler suddenly in the middle of the road without giving any signal or indications to other road users and he has also contributed more than 50% negligence, hence the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.

Respondent No.3 denied the age,
income, occupation of the petitioner and stated that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.
SCCH-25 7.

On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-1-MM-4326 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3.

What order or Award?
8.
The Petitioner in order to prove her case, has examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.11.
On the other side, the Respondent Nos.2 & 3 did not examine any witness nor produced any documents.

9. Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.
SCCH-25 10.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: In the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:-
REASONS 11. Issue No.1:-
Sudha Ravishankar vs Naveeen .N on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84711924/
3

In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MM-4326, the petitioner has examined herself as PW.1 by reiterating the petition averments in her chief examination affidavit and produced 7 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.7.
During her cross- examination she has admitted that she was going in Active Honda bearing No.KA-04-HX-4788 with her husband from palace Guttahalli to Doddanakundhi.
The offending vehicle was car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MM-4326.
Further admitted that as per Sketch the accident occurred in a junction.
SCCH-25 12
. The accident occurred on 09.11.2017 and the FIR was registered on the same day.
The Mahazar at Ex.P.2 was conducted on 10.11.2017 at about 09.00am to 10.00am.
The Sketch at Ex.P.3 shows that the accident occurred in the middle of the Road.
Ex . P.4
statement of witness gives the details of the accident through witness .
The Ex.P.5 Notice u/Sec.133 of MV Act sent to the RC owner about full details of the accident and also reply to that notice.
Wound Certificate at Ex.P.6 shows that the petitioner has suffered injuries in an RTA on 09.11.2017 at about 30.30pm.
Ex.P.7 MVA report shows that the vehicle bearing No.KA-04-HX-4788 damaged to its rear left side body.
The Respondent No.3 has contended that the accident occurred due to 50% contribution of the petitioner and the sole negligence of the rider of the Honda Activa.
But in order to prove the same they have neither produced any documents nor examined any witness.

Therefore, on the basis of the evidence of PW.1 and the documents before the court Exs.P.1 to P.7, the Tribunal holds that the SCCH-25 accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-01-MM-4326.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-
The Petitioner has further averred that on account of the accidental injury she is suffering from simple injuries of Abrasion left shoulder and contusion left ankle and foot.

The Petitioner to substantiate that there is loss of income due to the accidental injuries and that she is suffering from permanent disability has not examined either the treated Doctor or any other Doctor who has got expertise in this field.
She also has not placed any disability certificate issued by the competent person to prove that she suffered permanent disability.

Therefore, in absence of evidence this Tribunal holds that the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident has not caused her permanent disability resulting in loss of income and accordingly the version of the petitioner in this regard is not acceptable.
Under these SCCH-25 circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
However, it is pertinent to note that, the wound certificate produced as per Ex.P.6 discloses that, she has sustained simple injuries.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- under the head of Pain and Suffering.

The Petitioner has stated that she has spent more than Rs.10,000/-
medical, conveyance and nourishment expenses.

In this regard she has produced 3 Sudha Ravishankar vs Naveeen .N on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84711924/
4 medical bills for Rs.17,249/- as per Ex.P.9.
These medical bills are of 2024 and also not related to the injuries.
Therefore, petitioner is not entitled to any amount under the heads of medical expenses.
As mentioned above the Petitioner was treated at Vikram Hospital, Bangalore, wherein she was treated.
In this regard she has not produced any discharge summary of that hospital.
But, during that time, certainly she would have spent some amount towards attendant, conveyance, transportation and for other incidental expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is SCCH-25 entitled for a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards attendant, conveyance, transportation and other incidental expenses.
The total compensation comes to Rs.20,000/-.

14. LIABILITY:
As discussed above the Respondent Nos.2 & 3 have failed to prove its defence about the accident.
Therefore, the Respondents No.2 & 3 being the RC owner and the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.25,000/- but she is entitled only for a sum of Rs.20,000/-. alongwith interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.3:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
SCCH-25 ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/-. (Rupees Twenty Thousand only) along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount by the respondent (not entitled to interest from the date of order of dismissal for default i.e., 19.02.2021 till the date of restoration i.e.,
13.12.2023).
The Respondent Nos.2 & 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The Respondent No.3 being the insurer of the offending vehicle shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner through e-payment on proper SCCH-25 identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
